newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Suharto calls for closer Indonesian-Thai ties.
newsitem.headline: Suharto calls for closer Indonesian-Thai ties.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto called on Thursday for closer cooperation between his country and Thailand in the economic field, trade and technology.

Speaking at a state banquet he hosted for visiting Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, Suharto said Indonesia was closely watching Thailand's efforts to become a centre for trade, investment, finance and tourism in Southeast Asia.
"In this respect, both countries need to improve their cooperation, especially economic, trade and technical cooperation," he said in his prepared address.
"We have great potential to develop mutual bilateral cooperation to benefit the people of our two countries," he added.
Chavalit earlier arrived in Jakarta for a two-day visit and will have official talks with Suharto on Friday before leaving for home around midday (0500 GMT).
Indonesian officials and Thai diplomats said the talks would be general, covering various areas of cooperation, with no fundamental issues between the two countries.

Diplomatic sources said the visit was primarily a courtesy call, following a custom of new leaders of members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) to call first on fellow ASEAN states.
ASEAN comprises Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam.

During a formal welcoming ceremony, Suharto -- the region's elder statesman -- congratulated Chavalit on his election in November and said his visit reflected the good relations between their two countries.
In his banquet address, Suharto said Indonesia and Thailand cooperated well in the economic and political fields.
"In the economic field, our cooperation has shown steady development. There now are 26 Thai companies investing in Indonesia, while 12 Indonesian companies are investing in Thailand," he said.
Thailand is also interested in getting gas from Indonesia's huge Natuna field once it is developed in the South China Sea.
Suharto said ASEAN had benefited the nations of Southeast Asia, strengthening stability, boosting the region's economy and developing cooperation.
